en: Using an inclined ramp to move heavy boxes prevents back injuries because it reduces the lifting force your muscles need to apply.
Wearing rubber-soled shoes on wet floors prevents slipping because rubber increases friction between your feet and the slippery surface.
Wearing a bicycle helmet protects your head because gravity accelerates your falling body downward, increasing the impact force during a crash.
Keeping magnetic stripe cards away from strong neodymium magnets prevents data loss because the magnet's field alters the magnetic information on the strip.
Never touch electrical switches with wet hands because the dissolved minerals in tap water conduct electricity, which can send a dangerous shock through your body.
Looking directly at a solar eclipse without certified glasses can permanently damage your retina because intense visible and invisible light burns the eye tissue.
Wearing earplugs at loud concerts protects your hearing because prolonged exposure to sounds above 85 decibels permanently damages the tiny hair cells in your inner ear.
Using a silicone pot holder when lifting a hot pan prevents burns because silicone is a thermal insulator that blocks heat transfer to your skin.
Eating a banana before playing sports provides your body with chemical energy from carbohydrates that your muscles convert into kinetic energy for physical movement.
Wrapping yourself in a wool blanket keeps you warm because wool traps your body's thermal energy and prevents it from escaping into the cold air.
Unplugging appliances by pulling the hard plastic plug instead of the cord prevents internal wire damage that could cause a dangerous electrical short circuit.
Using a wheelbarrow to transport heavy garden soil uses a second-class lever and wheels to multiply your lifting force and reduce physical strain.
